title: Determining the Safety of CAR T-Cell Therapy for Lymphoma
official: Phase I Dose-Escalation/Expansion Study of Anti-CD19/CD22 CAR T-Cell Therapy for Relapsed/Refractory Mature B-cell Lymphoma After Prior CD19 CAR T-Cell Failure
summary: This study seeks to determine the safety of CAR T-cell therapy in participants with relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance status ≤ 2
* At least 1 measurable lesion according to the Lugano Response Criteria for Malignant Lymphoma70
* Measurable disease defined as ≥ 1 measurable nodal lesion (long axis \> 1.5 cm and short axis \> 1.0 cm) or ≥ 1 measurable extranodal lesion (long axis \> 1.0 cm) on computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
* Lesions that have been previously irradiated will be considered measurable only if progression has been documented following completion of radiation therapy
* Total bilirubin ≤ 2.0 mg/dL (or \< 3.0 mg/dL for subjects with Gilbert's syndrome or lymphomatous infiltration of the liver)
* Alanine aminotransferase (AST) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤ 3 x upper limit of normal (ULN); or ≤ 5 x ULN if known lymphomatous infiltration of the liver
* Creatinine clearance (as estimated by Cockcroft Gault) ≥ 30 mL/min
* Adequate cardiac function as defined by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≥ 40% as assessed by echocardiography, multigated acquisition scan (MUGA), or cardiac MRI
* Baseline oxygen saturation ≥ 92% on room air
* Adequate bone marrow function without growth factor support with short-acting G-CSF within the previous 7 days or long-acting G-CSF within the previous 14 days, and without transfusion support within 7 days prior to apheresis:
* Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1,000/microliter (µL)
* Absolute lymphocyte count (ALC) ≥ 100/microliter (µL)
* Platelets ≥ 50,000/microliter (µL)
* Hemoglobin ≥ 7g/dL
* Subjects must have the ability to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.

Exclusion Criteria:

* The presence of any of the following will exclude a subject from study enrollment:
* Presence of acute or extensive chronic graft versus host disease (GVHD).
* Active central nervous system or meningeal involvement by lymphoma. Subjects with untreated brain metastases/central nervous system (CNS) disease will be excluded from this clinical trial because of their poor prognosis and because they often develop progressive neurologic dysfunction that would confound the evaluation of neurologic and other adverse events. Patients with a history of CNS or meningeal involvement must be in a documented remission by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) evaluation and contrast-enhanced MRI imaging for at least 90 days prior to registration.
* History of another primary malignancy that has not been in remission for at least 2 years. The following are examples of exemptions from the 2-year limit: nonmelanoma skin cancer, definitively treated stage 1 solid tumor with low risk for recurrence, curatively treated localized prostate cancer, and cervical carcinoma in situ on biopsy or a squamous intraepithelial lesion on papanicolaou (PAP) smear, and in situ breast cancer that has been completely resected.
* HIV seropositivity.
* Subjects with uncontrolled intercurrent illness.
* Pregnant or breastfeeding women are excluded from this study because CAR T-cell therapy may be associated with the potential for teratogenic or abortifacient effects. Women of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test. Subjects of either sex who are not willing to practice birth control from the time of consent and at least 6 months after protocol-directed CAR T-cell infusion are excluded (see Section 9.6 for contraception method). Because there is an unknown, but potential risk for adverse events in nursing infants secondary to treatment of the mother with CAR T-cells, breastfeeding should be discontinued. These potential risks may also apply to other agents used in this study.
* Serologic status reflecting active hepatitis B or C infection. Patients that are positive for hepatitis B core antibody, hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), or hepatitis C antibody must have a negative polymerase chain reaction (PCR) prior to enrollment. (PCR positive patients will be excluded.)
* Presence of an active and clinically relevant CNS disorder such as epilepsy, generalized seizure disorders, paresis, aphasia, stroke, uncontrolled cerebrovascular disease, cerebellar disease, severe brain injuries, dementia and Parkinson's disease
* History of autoimmune disease (i.e. rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus) with requirement of immunosuppressive medication within 6 months.
* Patients who have received \>1 prior CAR T-cell infusion. Patients treated with multiple CAR T-cell infusions in the context of a prior prospective therapeutic clinical trial will be permitted.
* Any medical condition likely to interfere with assessment of safety or efficacy of study treatment
* History of severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction to tocilizumab, anakinra or any of the agents used in this study
* Major surgery within 28 days prior to start of lymphodepleting chemotherapy or any planned medical/surgical treatment that might interfere with the ability to comply with the study requirements.
* Patients must have a washout period of at least 2 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is shorter, since any prior cancer therapy, at the time the patient undergoes apheresis, except as follows:
* Treatment with alemtuzumab or bendamustine within 6 months of apheresis, or treatment with fludarabine, melphalan, or cladribine within 3 months of apheresis
* Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant within 12 weeks prior to apheresis
* Therapeutic doses of corticosteroids (defined as \> 20 mg/day prednisone or equivalent) within 5 days prior to apheresis. Physiologic replacement, topical, and inhaled steroids are permitted.
* Oral targeted agents, including lenalidomide and ibrutinib, are allowed if at least 3 half-lives have elapsed prior to apheresis.
* Experimental agents within 4 weeks of apheresis unless no response or disease progression is documented on the experimental therapy and at least 3 half-lives have elapsed prior to apheresis
* Radiation within 6 weeks of apheresis. Subjects must have progressive disease in irradiated lesions or have additional non-irradiated, PET-positive lesions to be eligible. Radiation to a single lesion or lesions, if additional non-irradiated PET-positive lesions are present, is allowed up to 2 weeks prior to apheresis.
* Prior cell, gene, or antibody-based therapy (approved or investigational) targeting both cluster of differentiation 19 (CD19) and cluster of differentiation 22 (CD22).
* Prior bispecific T-cell engaging antibody therapy targeting cluster of differentiation 20 (CD20), cluster of differentiation 19 (CD19), or cluster of differentiation 22 (CD22) on B-cells: a minimum of 30 days must have elapsed between the last dose of bispecific T-cell engaging antibody therapy and apheresis.
* CD19-directed CAR T-cell infusion within 12 weeks of planned apheresis.
* Prior cell, gene, or antibody-based therapy (approved or investigational) targeting both CD19 and CD22.
* Prior bispecific T-cell engaging antibody therapy targeting CD20, CD19, or CD22 on B-cells: a minimum of 30 days must have elapsed between the last dose of bispecific T-cell engaging antibody therapy and apheresis.
* CNS prophylaxis (e.g., intrathecal methotrexate): must be stopped at least 1 week prior to apheresis
* Treatment with systemic immunostimulatory agents (including, but not limited to, interferon and interleukin-2 \[IL-2\]) within 6 weeks or 5 half-lives of the drug, whichever is shorter, prior to apheresis.
